tasks.short: Check consent, then call owners to solicit a sales listing.

steps.what: Check consent before any call to property owners.
Decide which services to offer this owner on the call.
Contact the owner and solicit sales listings.
Send the agreed services. Do not advertise beyond them.
Log the listing lead or the owner's refusal.

tasks.design: The {CRM} shows whether this owner may be called. The agent decides the services on offer, makes the call, and a follow-up names only those services. The call is not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Owner lists were dialled from a spreadsheet, with consent assumed.
tasks.enabler_now: A consent field and a date can block a call. The call itself stays a conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing, on the call, whether the owner wants to sell or wants the calls to stop.
tasks.human_edge: The agent drops a number the moment consent is missing or withdrawn.

ambition.what: Every owner is marked callable or not before the dial, including people who were clients before.

tasks.altitude: The calls stay. The agent can refuse a list that has no consent record, and can refuse a follow-up that advertises a service they did not offer.

reach.task: Set which services an agent may offer on a listing call
reach.learn: Which promises the broker will not let a call make

evidence.claim: Calls to consumers, including existing customers, need a prior consent record.
Recording calls in a way that can monitor staff needs works-council consent. This design does not record the call.
A consent flag can stop a dial. The conversation stays with the agent.

assumptions: Focal role is the sales agent. Boundary: from an owner record to a lead or a refusal. Bought lists are out of scope unless a consent record is stored.
Fields: owner name, phone, consent yes or no, consent date, and the services the agent may name. The owner produces the yes or no on the call. Fallback: do not call.
Configure the consent field on the contact before a new dialler. Upkeep of 3 hours covers the service list.
The class is human. The call share stays. The design disagrees with any prior that treats the dial as automatic.
unknowns: What share of owner numbers already have a consent date.
Whether the office buys contact lists.
research_questions: What share of listing calls end in a refusal to be called again?

incremental.description: Review the service list the follow-up is allowed to name

approvals.approved_version: consent record and offer limits for that owner
service sheet agreed on the call

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: consent is missing on most numbers, so the task shrinks to checking and stopping. High: consented owners are called as today, and only the log and the follow-up shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Call previous clients for referrals only where consent still holds.

steps.what: List previous clients whose matter closed over a year ago.
Confirm consent still covers a referral call.
Contact previous clients and ask for referral business.
Record the referral or a request not to call.

tasks.design: A {CRM} list proposes previous clients. The agent clears consent, then calls. A request not to be called is stored. The call is not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Previous clients were rung from memory, as if an old sale was permanent consent.
tasks.enabler_now: Close dates are fields. Consent for a new call is not implied by an old sale.
tasks.still_hard: Asking for a referral without making a former client feel used.
tasks.human_edge: The agent hears a no and stops, including a soft no.

ambition.what: Former clients who asked not to be called are treated as a group the office no longer prospects.

tasks.altitude: The calls stay. The agent can refuse a list that treats an old sale as consent.

reach.task: Ask a former client for an introduction
reach.learn: How a no is recorded so the next caller sees it

evidence.claim: The consent rule for calls includes existing customers, not only strangers.
This design does not record the call, because recording that can monitor staff needs works-council consent.

assumptions: Focal role is the sales agent. Boundary: from closed matters to a referral or a do-not-call mark. Prospecting is this call, not a campaign to strangers.
Fields: client name, matter close date, consent, and do-not-call. The client produces the referral or the refusal. Fallback: leave them off the list.
Use the contact record before a new list. Upkeep of 2 hours covers the do-not-call review.
The class is human. Existing customers are not exempt from the consent check.
unknowns: Whether old files store any consent at all.
How long after a sale the office usually calls.
research_questions: What share of previous clients ask not to be called?

incremental.description: Review do-not-call marks so a later list does not revive them

approvals.approved_version: referral call list the agent cleared

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most files have no consent, so the work is the check and the stop. High: cleared clients are still called in full, and only the list-making shrinks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep a referral network and introduce a client only with consent.

steps.what: Update cards for attorneys, mortgage lenders and contractors.
Pick which of the networks fits this client's problem.
Confirm the client wants the introduction before it is sent.
Send the introduction the client has just accepted.
Accept or decline the referred client.
Develop the networks only after meeting the person.

tasks.design: Partner cards live on the {CRM}. The agent picks a name, asks the client, and the introduction goes only after that yes. Adding a person to the network still requires a meeting. The attorney's accept or decline is their time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Introductions went by a personal mail, and the client sometimes heard about it afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: A card can hold a name and a trade. Sending a client's name is still a disclosure.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing which attorney actually fits, and which one the client will trust.
tasks.human_edge: The agent will not send a client's name to a person the client has not accepted.

ambition.what: Each introduction is a yes from the client on that name, not a habit.

tasks.altitude: Meetings with new partners stay. The agent can withhold an introduction, and can drop a card after a bad outcome.

reach.role: securities and financial services sales agent
reach.task: Pass a client to a specialist
reach.learn: What the client must agree before their name is sent

evidence.claim: Sending a client's name to another professional is a disclosure and needs a reason the client knows about.
A contact card can store a trade and a name. Choosing the person stays with the agent.

assumptions: Focal role is the sales agent. Boundary: from partner cards to an introduction the client accepted, or to a card kept after a meeting. The attorney's reply is supplier time.
Fields: name, trade, and the matter types they take. The client produces the yes. Fallback: do not send.
Configure contact cards before a new directory. Upkeep of 4 hours covers cards that go stale.
A referral of a person is personal data. The design does not score partners.
unknowns: Whether clients already sign a referral consent.
How many names the office considers current.
research_questions: What share of introductions does the client refuse?

incremental.description: Drop partner cards the office no longer stands behind

approvals.approved_version: introduction the client accepted and the agent chose

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the work is the meeting and the client's yes, which stay. High: cards are current and the sending itself is a short step. The attorney's time is not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order a title search, read the result, then tell the client.

steps.what: Arrange the title searches from the clients property address.

loop.input: Address and buyer names on the deal
loop.check: Agent corrects a name or address the file does not show
loop.why_not_simpler: Addresses in prose do not always match the register

steps.what: Submit the approved title order to the registry.
Run the title searches and return the result pack.
Read the result and determine whether the title looks clear.
Tell the clients what the title result means for them.

tasks.design: The order is filled from the deal, submitted to the {GOV_PORTAL} only after the agent checks the names, and read by the agent when it returns. The title office does the search. The client is told only the reading the agent signed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders were retyped, and a result was sometimes forwarded unread.
tasks.enabler_now: Name and address can fill an order. Reading a charge on a title cannot be a rule.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing a restriction that is real even when the summary line says clear.
tasks.human_edge: The agent will not tell a client the title is clear without reading the result.

ambition.what: Each result is marked clear, unclear or needs a lawyer before the client is told.

tasks.altitude: Reading stays. The agent can hold an explanation that is not the reading they signed, and can refuse to forward a raw result.

reach.task: See a title defect that changes what cover can be discussed
reach.learn: Which defects must be handed to a lawyer before anyone talks about cover

evidence.claim: An order form can be filled from name and address. Judging whether a title is clear stays with a person.

assumptions: Focal role is the sales agent. Boundary: from a deal address to an explanation of the title result. The search itself is the title office's time and is not saved.
Fields: client names and the property address as stored. The title office produces the result. Fallback: the agent types the address when the field is blank.
Use the {GOV_PORTAL} the registry already offers before a private copy of the register. Upkeep of 3 hours covers order fields.
Identifiers are often messy. The design assumes the agent still reads every result. The class is human.
unknowns: Whether the registry accepts an electronic order from an agent.
research_questions: What share of results contain a charge the summary line did not show?

incremental.description: Keep order fields aligned with what the registry asks for

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: addresses are messy and every result is read in full, so little shrinks. High: the order and the sending shrink, the reading stays, and the title office's time is not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Listing calls, referral calls, partner meetings and title reading stay. Nothing is sent until consent or a signed reading exists.
reach: Insurance sales agents: notice a title defect or a do-not-call mark before they start their own conversation
skills_to_grow: Stopping a call that has no consent record
Asking the client before their name is sent
Reading a title result without calling it clear from the summary line
role.ambitious_version: No listing call and no referral call go out without a consent record, and no client is told a title is clear before the agent has read the result.
